title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## ForceWAM: Decoupled Future & Response Learning

### The Breakthrough
The paper introduces ForceWAM, a force‑world‑action model that separates prediction of task‑compatible interaction outcomes from learning how local actions affect contact. It trains a world model on demonstration video and six‑axis wrench trajectories and an inverse‑dynamics model on both demonstrations and play data, enabling reactive control on a real robot. Experiments achieve 85‑95 % mean success on sliding, box‑flipping, and ring‑placement tasks, surpassing prior baselines.

### The Caveats
The work only demonstrates success on three specific tasks and never evaluates on unseen objects or tasks, leaving its claim of general applicability unsubstantiated.

## LoopWAM: Closed‑Loop Policy Improvement

### The Breakthrough
LoopWAM is a closed‑loop world‑action model that learns from the full spectrum of real‑world rollout data, including successes, suboptimal actions, and failures. By unifying behavior imitation with action‑conditioned world modeling and using quality‑weighted supervision, it raises RoboChallenge Table30‑V2 success from 23.67 % to 43.33 % and reaches 94.5 % average success on RoboTwin 2.0.

### The Caveats
The reported success gains lack any baseline or competing closed‑loop method comparison, so it’s unclear whether LoopWAM itself is responsible for the improvement.

## ILA: Interaction Latents as Actions

### The Breakthrough
ILA treats learned interaction latents as the robot’s action primitive, jointly encoding motion, contact, and force via a visually‑conditioned joint action‑tactile reconstruction and an implicit decoder. The latents serve as flow‑matching targets for vision‑language‑action models and policies, yielding large gains over tactile‑conditioned baselines on four real‑world tasks.

### The Caveats
The claimed broader applicability rests on results from just four known tasks, with no tests on unseen tasks, objects, or larger benchmark suites to demonstrate generalization.

## ChunkAct: Action Chunking for LLM Robots

### The Breakthrough
ChunkAct groups consecutive robot primitives into a single LLM‑driven action chunk, returning control only on failure, which cuts LLM calls by 2.9×, input tokens by 4.4×, and output tokens by 2.3× while raising LIBERO‑Pro success by 5 points over prior agentic‑robotics methods.

### The Caveats
The paper never names or compares against any existing baselines, so the reported 5‑point boost on LIBERO‑Pro cannot be verified against current state‑of‑the‑art methods.

## Tesla Robotaxi Speeding Allegation

### The Breakthrough
A petition to NHTSA alleges that about 1,000 Tesla Model Y robotaxis and Cybercabs exceed speed limits in active school zones, citing three video links and social‑media reports as evidence.

### The Caveats
The allegation relies solely on three videos and social‑media reports, without any systematic traffic‑safety data or independent verification.

## LeRobot 100TB+ Streaming Loader

### The Breakthrough
LeRobot released an episode‑based streaming loader that reads robot demonstration videos and tables directly from Hugging Face datasets or cloud buckets, enabling training on datasets exceeding 100 TB without a full local copy and achieving 200 samples / s throughput.

### The Caveats
The loader’s impressive throughput numbers are presented without any baseline or prior‑art data‑loader comparison, leaving its real advantage unverified.

## Humxn $50M Skilled Trades Data

### The Breakthrough
Humxn Research Labs announced a $50 million program to purchase real‑world service records, photos, videos and manuals from skilled trades and license the curated datasets to AI and robotics developers, paying workers $20 per hour of wearable‑camera footage.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no independent verification of the data’s quality, scale, or any demonstrated impact on robotics performance, making the claimed benefits unsubstantiated.

## Physical Intelligence API Beta

### The Breakthrough
Physical Intelligence launched a beta API that offers cloud‑hosted training and inference for large robotic foundation models (ϵ0 and ϵ0.5), letting developers upload data, fine‑tune, and run policies on robots via a managed gateway.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no quantitative benchmarks or baseline comparisons, so the claimed breadth and performance of the Pi API remain unverified.

## SAM3DBody‑cpp: Real‑Time 3D Pose Engine

### The Breakthrough
The SAM3DBody‑cpp repository delivers a standalone C++ inference engine that converts a single‑camera BGR image into 70‑joint skeletons, optional mesh vertices, and BVH or MPEG‑ARF avatar exports, using an ONNX‑compiled DINOv3‑ViT‑H/14+ encoder and YOLO11m pose detector for near‑real‑time GPU performance.

### The Caveats
The repository reports no quantitative accuracy or benchmark results and cites no prior pose‑estimation baselines, leaving its claimed real‑time 3D pose quality entirely unverified.

## OpenHarness: Multi‑Agent Coding Hub

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness is an open‑source TypeScript app that runs multiple coding agents (Claude, Codex, Copilot, etc.) in separate tmux panes across machines, connecting them via encrypted WebRTC channels with latency of 11‑13 ms median and CPU usage of ~0.1 % of a core.

### The Caveats
The reported latency and CPU usage are presented without any baseline comparison to existing IDEs or multi‑agent frameworks, so it’s unclear whether OpenHarness actually outperforms current tools.

## LearnOpt Motion Planning Suite

### The Breakthrough
LearnOpt_Motion_Planning bundles a variety of optimization‑based planners and reinforcement‑learning controllers for quadrotor navigation in MuJoCo, including FIRI corridor construction, GCOPTER/MINCO trajectory optimization, GCS graph‑based planning, YOPO end‑to‑end planning, and an Actor‑Critic MPC layer that learns a neural cost map via PPO.

### The Caveats
The repository provides no baseline or benchmark comparisons, so the claimed simulation improvements remain unverified.

### Priority
ForceWAM stands out as the most concrete hardware result today, showing how decoupling future prediction from reactive control can dramatically boost success on contact‑rich manipulation tasks.

### One action
Try reproducing the ForceWAM pipeline on your own robot arm to evaluate its 85‑95 % success claim on a simple sliding task.

### What to watch
Four recent papers (ForceWAM, LoopWAM, ILA, and ChunkAct) explore different angles on improving contact‑rich manipulation—from decoupled world models and closed‑loop rollout learning to latent‑action representations and LLM‑driven action chunking. Their overlapping goals suggest a rapid convergence on hybrid perception‑force pipelines, and future benchmarks may compare these approaches head‑to‑head.
